inspiration: Base as a placed-object list: each object has a type, a position, a yaw, an id and a map id, so a whole base is data, not code (zonemaps/map01.json first entry lines 2-12). Recreate the schema for our zones with our own object types.

Base vocabulary: a small set of recurring object types (storage lockers, terminals, a respawn tube, a turret, a zipline, doors with interior and exterior versions) makes each base read the same way at a glance. Keep the repeat, change the forms (zonemaps/map01.json types, count table in the md).

Link graph per zone: a pair list per map says which bases connect, and a separate list links the zones (lattice.json; Zones.scala lines 417-420, 749-753). Keep the two-tier graph: local links per zone and one inter-zone list. Use for spawn routes and travel.

Toggled hazard volume: a sphere sitting slightly below the surface, an always-on flag that can be off, and a fixed small damage that hits health only (GlobalDefinitionsMiscellaneous.scala lines 861-870). Keep the toggle and the health-only rule; change the shape to a ring and the cadence to a visible pulse.

Respawn point as an object with a fixed delay field (ams_respawn_tube.Delay = 10 with a comment that 10 is temporary, default 1; GlobalDefinitionsMiscellaneous.scala lines 38-40). Keep a respawn delay as a field on the spawn object; change to our zone timing.

Overlay overrides: a separate list of per-item property overrides laid on top of base definitions (overrides/*.adb.lst). Keep the overlay layering for our balance values, change the values and the format.
Id pools per zone: a start and a max per pool so entity ids in different zones never collide (guid-pools/c1.json). Keep the block-per-zone rule; change the sizes.

briefs.label: Respawn pod with a delay
briefs.why: A visible pod that brings a player back after a set wait gives every death a clear next step.
briefs.keep: spawn point as an object with one delay field; a spawn-tube object placed in the zone that the player steps into
briefs.change: our own pod shape and material; a countdown shown on the pod; a different delay per zone

briefs.label: Toggled hazard ring
briefs.why: A hazard that can be switched on and off and hits health only reads as a rule the player can learn.
briefs.keep: always-on flag that can be off; sphere offset below the surface; small fixed damage to health only
briefs.change: ring shape instead of sphere; a pulse light on each tick; our own damage type

briefs.label: Two-tier base graph
briefs.why: A link list per zone plus one list between zones gives travel and spawn routes without code per route.
briefs.keep: pair list per zone; separate inter-zone list; links read from data at load
briefs.change: our zone names; links drawn as a road or a river; a cost per link

briefs.label: Zipline traversal
briefs.why: A fast drop between two points changes how a map is read and gives a second route.
briefs.keep: two fixed ends; a one-way or two-way use; a fast ride between them
briefs.change: a rope bridge or vine instead of a steel cable; our own ride speed and sound
briefs.ref: src/main/resources/zonemaps/map01.json (ObjectType zipline; grep for it, lines not checked)
